title: Deferred ingest canonicalization and billing merge to avoid double-charge on concurrent retries
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: at-least-once ingestion from diverse clients (SDKs, edge proxies) combined with concurrent retries and network timeouts is causing duplicated token billing in ~0.05% of high-throughput customer workloads. Existing mitigations (opaque replay tokens, client-side dedupe) reduce but don't eliminate duplicates because: (1) some SDKs crash before persisting replay tokens, (2) edge proxies short-circuit and retry, and (3) multi-path requests hit different frontends before global dedupe converges.

Proposal: introduce a deferred ingest canonicalization stage and a billing-merge step that ensures accounting is done against a canonicalized request instance. High-level flow: (A) Accept ingest as provisional with an ingest-anchor (client-supplied or server-assigned) and return provisional-ack to lower latency; (B) Asynchronously canonicalize within a configurable compaction window (default 1500ms) using a canonicalization pipeline (hash on normalized prompt + model+params + client anchor), grouping near-identical requests to one canonical record; (C) On canonical record commit, commit a single billing event into the consumption ledger and mark all provisional accepts as merged; (D) Provide an external reconciliation API and periodic sweep for late arrivals (up to 24h) to prevent permanent divergence.

Why different from prior approaches: this does not require global synchronous consensus at request time (keeps p99 latency low), but ensures eventual single-billing semantics. It handles crashy clients and multi-path routing by relying on a short, well-defined compaction window and a deterministic canonicalization function.

Key design details: canonicalization key = SHA256(normalize(prompt) || model || stringified_params || customer_id || optional_client_anchor). Normalization rules are conservative (whitespace collapse, canonical JSON for structured inputs) to minimize false merges. Storage: implement canonical index as a sharded RocksDB store per region with local LRU bloom filter to limit lookups. The canonical commit writes an idempotent billing marker to the per-customer compacted ledger (append-only, sequence-numbered) which downstream billing jobs will consume.

Failure modes and trade-offs: increases background work and short-lived state; risk of false merges (merge two semantically different prompts that normalize the same) — mitigated by conservative normalization and a manual rollback path that can split charges within 24h. Adds a small window where provisional-ack may be visible to callers as completed before billing commit; we will clearly document provisional semantics in SDKs.

Monitoring and SLOs: track duplicate_charge_rate (target < 0.001%), false_merge_rate (target < 0.0001%), canonicalization_latency_p50/p99, reconcile_sweep_lag. Add dashboard widgets in Console and an alert when duplicate_charge_rate > 0.005% for > 10m.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Build canonicalization library (normalize + hash) and unit tests (ENG).
2) Implement sharded canonical index service + local bloom filters (ENG).
3) Add provisional-ack response path and provisional state store (edge/frontends) that references canonicalization id.
4) Implement billing-merge writer in consumption service and idempotent commit semantics.
5) Reconciliation sweep job + admin tooling to inspect merged groups and split charges.
6) SDK updates to surface provisional flags and allow client-supplied anchor.
7) Gradual rollout: internal dogfood customers -> opt-in beta customers -> default-on for new accounts.

Expected rollout timeline: development and tests 3w, canary 2w, full rollout 2w.

Open questions: acceptable compaction window for enterprise workloads? (Investor-facing latency vs billing correctness). Should we prioritize server-assigned anchors (safer) or encourage client anchors (faster dedupe)? Current proposal supports both with server anchor fallback.
